activity_context.topic_title: Calculating Areas of Right Triangles Using Trigonometry

feedback.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14070169/assets/7e555f1574ba37c5b2ac8f4bca54f0d9e2b449e1351f792feba334ddbdc5b8df.png)

Given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\sqrt{3},$ the **exact** area of $△ABC$ shown above is{{field-1}} square units.
feedback.worked_solution:
In this case, the area of the right triangle is

$$
A=\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC.
$$

We are given that $\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B)=\sqrt{3}.$ Notice that relative to $∠B,$ we have expressions for the lengths of the opposite side $\overset{―}{AC}$ and adjacent side $\overset{―}{BC}.$ Hence, we can use the tangent ratio to solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(m∠B) & =\frac{AC}{BC} \\ \sqrt{3} & =\frac{\sqrt{3}(x-4)}{8-x} \\ \sqrt{3}(8-x) & =\sqrt{3}(x-4) \\ 8-x & =x-4 \\ 2x & =12 \\ x & =6\end{aligned}
$$

So, the side lengths are

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =8-x=8-6=2, \\ AC & =\sqrt{3}(x-4)=\sqrt{3}(6-4)=2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of $△ABC$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot AC \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot 2\cdot 2\sqrt{3} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$
